report.notes: 9 new tests (test_r1r2_*) in tests/dev_workflow/test_lifecycle.py: all 9 fail on fbac437 (checked via git archive copy, since git worktree add was declined) and pass after; full tests/dev_workflow suite 161 passed. R1-01: verdict parsed from in-memory result_text (result_sha256 = its hash); round.json hash taken from the written bytes; verify() re-derives each round's result from the hashed stdout (claude_cli JSON 'result' extraction mirrored) and checks reviewer_result.txt against result_sha256; §6 limitation text corrected and the correction recorded in LIFECYCLE_QUALIFICATION.md. R1-02: result_problem() makes a non-list or non-dict findings/prior_findings result unparseable (NO_RESULT -> WAITING_FOR_MODEL; effective_verdict returns None), also for import-review. Missing finding id is not required, because the existing test_r1_09 uses id-less findings and missing severity is already blocking. R1-03: _test_file maps junit classnames (strips trailing class components) and resolves paths against the gate cwd then the repo root; _commit_and_prove refuses a gate repair whose named test is not a file with a configured runner; regression_proof reports must_fail tests that were not run; __run__ gate findings carry no file. R1-04: control_state (hooks/config/info digest + refs/replace set) is bound in the PLAN event (CONTROL_ANCHORED for legacy runs) and checked before every step, after every review and in evidence_ok; any drift -> BLOCKED TAMPER with GIT_CONTROL marker, and only unblock of that block re-anchors; the diagnosis worker gets a before/after snapshot (refs, control, impl worktree) and tamper -> BLOCKED TAMPER; GIT adds -c core.fsmonitor=false. Not done: milestone refs are not anchored to PLAN because they move legitimately (still checked per step); a filter driver planted via config+attributes could still run during the post-review git status before drift is detected (detected right after, not prevented; not verified); graphify update not run because graphify-out/ is outside the permitted paths.
